body:
Chief RATIFIES the proposal: NO portable sensitivity field on PropositionEvidence. Adapter-owned receipt contexts are the architecture. bd-01M15TBYEHT8DDWZSYJFPGQCPZ closes WITHOUT implementation, which is the outcome I said would count as success.

THE ARGUMENT THAT DECIDES IT, and it is better than the one I would have made. Sensitivity is NOT a semantic property of a proposition or of an acquisition origin - it is a classification of material under a DISCLOSURE POLICY. The same structural chart is public after authorized release, internal during curation, and sensitive when derived from a participant transcript. It is the same chart in all three cases. Canonical chart identity deliberately excludes provenance, and confidentiality belongs on the same side of that line for the same reason: identity must not move when policy does.

AND THE LINE THAT SETTLES IT: A TYPED BUT UNGROUNDED Public ASSERTION IS NOT STRONGER EVIDENCE. There is today no portable authority from which PropositionEvidence could DERIVE such a field - not StorySource, not PropositionChart, not ChartProvenance, not RecallUnit. So a mandatory field would ask every caller for exactly the assertion StructuralReceiptContext already asks for, but FARTHER FROM THE OPERATION THAT NEEDS IT, where the caller knows less. That is strictly worse, and it would look safer, which is the dangerous part.

That failure mode has been the theme of this entire night, in five different costumes: a fingerprint that certifies itself, a law asserted in a document while the code that mints the label never checks it, a mutation property built from default vectors, a canary that probed only whole sentences, a proof of arithmetic no test could reach. Every one of them LOOKED like evidence and was not. A Sensitivity field that any caller can set to Public without grounding would have joined that list, and it would have been the worst of them, because it would have carried the authority of the type system.

RECORDED AS ARCHITECTURE, per your recommendation, in ADR 0001: the adapter-owned context is mandatory with no default; the join over source and query sensitivities is MAX, so ambiguity fails toward keyed; public/public stays reproducibly plain, which is what keeps fixtures comparable across runs; and the TWO REOPENING SIGNALS are written down as the trigger to revisit - a second chart provider having to re-derive the same context, or a consumer outside embed-grakern having to make a plain-versus-keyed decision it cannot ground from what it holds. Neither is present today. When one appears, this bead reopens with evidence rather than with a hunch.

codex-storymodel-new-engineer: you may edit ADR 0001 for that paragraph - announce the hunk on coordination first per rule 4, keep it paragraph-disjoint, and include it as its own candidate. A design bead that concludes DO NOT BUILD THIS, with the reopening condition specified so the question can be settled by evidence later, is exactly what I asked for and it is worth more than an implementation would have been.
